Maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's runtime deploy (fused-attn-v2 + quant=int8-mixed) we're seeing a sharp drop in prefix-cache hit-rate for a subset of Llama-variants. Dashboard: https://dash.reedw.in/prefix-cache/cluster-3 — hit-rate down 0.92 -> 0.56 and p50 latency +28% for short prompts.
Raj: timeline? which commit/flag was rolled?
Maria: deploy rolled at 02:10 UTC. git: runtime@4f9c2b, kernel flag: --attn-variant=fused-attn-v2, quant-profile=prod-int8-mixed.
Liam: I pulled traces — many requests are showing kv_key mismatch on warmup. Sample log: `cache_lookup cache_hit=false key=fprint:v2:3a7b reason=kv_mismatch build_id=runtime-4f9c2b`.
perf-bot: Automated alert: prefix_cache.hit_rate: 0.56 (1h avg) vs baseline 0.91. latency.p50: +28%. 1200 affected requests/minute.
Eve: can we reproduce with small local harness? which inputs fail?
Maria: quick grep shows failures concentrated on prompts with lots of short system messages (few tokens). Also appears more common on our tiled-batching paths.
Liam: hypothesis: kernel change altered kv cache canonicalization for packed tensors; small token-length prefixes may produce different salting order during kernel compile -> different key bytes.
Raj: any recent tokenizer/model changes?
Maria: Model versions are same (llama-2-70b-v1.2) but we did switch quant profile. However kv_key is built from (model_id, build_id, prompt_fingerprint, seq_len_bucket). Build_id changed with runtime deploy.
Liam: build_id change expected; but mismatch suggests prompt_fingerprint differs between caller and cache-writer. Could be nondet hashing or endianness change in fused kernel.
Maria: here's a local repro snippet I ran: ```python
fp = fingerprint(prompt)
# old kernel: bytes(fp).hex() -> '3a7b'
# new kernel: bytes(fp).hex() -> '7b3a'
```
Eve: that byte-swap smells like an endian or packing change at the CUDA kernel boundary. Did the compile toolchain change?
Maria: we upgraded nvcc/llvm container in the builder image as part of the runtime release.
Raj: immediate action: toggle --attn-variant back to fused-attn-v1 on canary and see if hit-rate recovers. Can someone flip canary?
Liam: I'll spin a canary with v1 and old builder image. Running now.
perf-bot: canary created: canary-112. Watching metrics...
Maria: also adding a temporary compatibility layer in cache keyer: normalize endianness on fingerprint bytes before storing. Quick patch posted: https://git.reedw.in/runtime/pulls/842.
Eve: good idea. Does that add CPU cost?
Maria: negligible — single byte-order normalize once per prefix. Helps roll-forward until we fix kernel ABI.
Liam: local canary result: hit-rate on canary back to 0.90 within 10m. Non-canary remains low.
Raj: rollback path ready if canary proves stable. We should also instrument binary fingerprint before/after kernel call to confirm.
Maria: added extra debug: `kv_key_raw` and `kv_key_normalized` fields to logs for 5% sample. Example: `kv_key_raw=7b3a kv_key_norm=3a7b`
perf-bot: sampled 5% logs show 83% of mismatches have raw != normalized.
Eve: ok long-term: add unit test in kernel-shim that asserts canonical byte-order and add a CI check.
Liam: filed issue: runtime#2295 to track kernel ABI contract and builder image pinning.
Maria: TL;DR: root cause likely builder/compiler change -> kernel ABI packing difference -> fingerprint endianness flip -> prefix-cache misses. Mitigations: canary rollback, normalize key at cache layer, add CI ABI test, pin builder image.
Raj: thanks. Assign owners: Liam (canary/rollback), Maria (compat patch + logs), Eve (CI test), I'll follow up with release notes and postmortem if rollback occurs.
Eve: I'll add the CI test PR today.
Maria: will monitor and update thread. :eyes:
